trip.name: An antiques-and-history day in Carson City
trip.description: A one-day itinerary on North Carson Street, mostly on foot: Carson Antiques & Collectibles Mall when it opens at 10 AM, the Nevada State Museum in the old Carson City Mint, the Nevada State Capitol and the Kit Carson Trail, then back to the mall for a second look before it closes at 6 PM.

sources: Stop addresses and distances from the mall's door (Children's Museum 813 N Carson St, 0.6 mi / about a 15-min walk; Nevada State Museum 600 N Carson St, 0.7 mi / 15-min walk; Capitol 101 N Carson St, 0.9 mi / 20-min walk; Carson Hot Springs 1500 Old Hot Springs Rd, 2 mi / 10-min drive; Railroad Museum 2180 S Carson St, 2.2 mi / 10-min drive; Stewart 1 Jacobsen Way, 5 mi / 15-min drive) and the Children's Museum's hands-on exhibits: the homepage's §5.3 source table (index.html, #day-trip comment). Never recomputed; the walk back reuses the Capitol figure.

Hours, 21,000 sq ft on two floors, upstairs, numbered booths by different vendors, cashier at the entrance, Treasure Map, Currency booths (coins in labeled holders in a lit case marked Coins, per the photo), railroad lantern: brand.md + store photos, as on the homepage.
Suzy C. quote: Google review, quoted verbatim on the homepage.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carson_City_Mint — coins struck 1870–1893 from Comstock Lode silver; CC mint mark on 50 silver and 57 gold issues; Morgan dollars rare and carry a premium; Abraham Curry construction supervisor, Father of Carson City, first superintendent; Coin Press No. 1 strikes commemorative CC medallions; museum in the building since 1941.

https://www.carsonnvmuseum.org/permanent-exhibits/ — Coin Press No. 1 and a complete set of Carson City Morgan dollars on display; a Columbian mammoth found in Nevada's Black Rock Desert; a tour of the underground mine.
https://www.carsonnvmuseum.org/location-hours-admission — the coin press operates on set days (the page names the day; we print set days, never other places' hours).

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_State_Capitol — built 1869–1871; sandstone from the Nevada State Prison quarry, free of charge; octagonal dome topped with a cupola; historical exhibits on the second floor; every governor except the first has had his office there.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carson_City,_Nevada — capital since 1861 (territory); Frémont named the Carson River for Kit Carson; Curry bought Eagle Station in 1858 and renamed it Carson City; for much of its history a hub of the Virginia and Truckee Railroad.

https://visitcarsoncity.com/attractions/kit-carson-trail/ — 2.5-mile path through the historic district; 48 stops incl. the Orion Clemens House and the Governor's Mansion; downloadable map; self-guided audio tour on any smartphone; begin wherever you like.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orion_Clemens — Mark Twain's older brother; first and only Secretary of the Nevada Territory.
https://visitcarsoncity.com/things-to-do/things-to-do-railroads/ — the railroad carried ore from the mines to the mills along the Carson River.
https://www.carsonrailroadmuseum.org/ — train rides on select weekends, holidays and special events; 2180 South Carson Street.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada_State_Railroad_Museum — V&T locomotives and cars; Dayton (V&T #18), built 1873, on display; Wabuska station on the grounds sells the ride tickets.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stewart_Indian_School — American Indian boarding school 1890–1980; buildings of colored local stone by student apprentices; cultural center opened 2020; walking tour of the former campus.

https://vtrailway.com/ — Carson City–Virginia City excursions from the Eastgate Depot, May through October, with a stop to explore Virginia City; holiday train November–December. Year not stated on the page.
https://vtrailway.com/know-before-you-go/ — Eastgate Depot, 4650 Eastgate Siding Road, Carson City.
